idiom_name: delegated properties over a Map (val x by map) with MutableMap for var
implementation_notes: Kotlin's documented 'storing properties in a map' delegation is the local idiom: `val name: String by map` reads map["name"] through the stdlib getValue(thisRef, property) extension, so the map is the property list and the property names are the indicators; `var` needs a MutableMap and writes through setValue. Only declared properties get dot access and they are cast to the declared type, so a genuinely open key set still uses the map API directly - the compiler cannot invent members. The classic owner/list structure is replaced rather than implemented, which is why the idiom is worth it when a known key set is filled from JSON or another dynamic source.
pitfalls: The map is keyed by the property name, so renaming the Kotlin property silently changes the wire key, and a missing key makes Map.getValue throw NoSuchElementException on first read (it throws when the key is absent even if the value would be null).

Delegation covers declared properties only - a genuinely new name at run time needs the map API or reflection (KClass.memberProperties) - and the delegated value is cast to the declared type, so a mismatched entry raises ClassCastException.
For var you must hold a MutableMap, and delegating several properties to one mutable map makes them views of shared state: any external write appears through the property.
